blocks.raw: # Configure SMS Settings
blocks.text: Configure SMS Settings

blocks.raw: For any organization to send SMS messages, it must first **register with telecom operators** through authorized gateways. This registration ensures that the sender's identity is verified and that messages comply with telecom regulations. Without this process, SMS traffic will not be delivered.

blocks.raw: ## Configuring communication and gateway settings
blocks.text: Configuring communication and gateway settings

blocks.raw: To send SMS, you need to connect Capillary with an SMS vendor, which is the service that delivers SMS to customers. The vendor manages the delivery of both bulk campaigns and transactional messages (such as OTPs and order confirmations).
blocks.text: To send SMS, you need to connect Capillary with an SMS vendor, which is the service that delivers SMS to customers. The vendor manages the delivery of both bulk campaigns and transactional messages (such as OTPs and order confirmations).

blocks.raw: You can either use Capillary’s supported vendors or <Anchor label="integrate a new vendor into the Capillary system" target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/vendor-integration-other-than-supported-vendors">integrate a new vendor into the Capillary system</Anchor> of your choice. To send SMS via any vendor, ensure that your message templates are approved on the DLT portal as per TRAI regulations. The supported SMS vendors are ICS, Airtel, Alibaba, Sinch, Onextel, Cequence, SolutionInfini, Tanla, Broadnet, Infobip, SSL, ValueFirst, TBP, Vectramind, Unicel, and Karix. To use any of these vendors, create a ticket to the Gateway team.

blocks.raw: ## Configuring the domain settings
blocks.text: Configuring the domain settings

blocks.raw: ### Prerequisites
blocks.text: Prerequisites

blocks.raw: * Obtain the **Sender Tag**, **GSM sender ID**, **GSM Sender Name**, **CDMA Sender ID**, and **CDMA Sender Name** from the brand.
blocks.text: Obtain the Sender Tag, GSM sender ID, GSM Sender Name, CDMA Sender ID, and CDMA Sender Name from the brand.

blocks.raw: Steps to configure the domain
blocks.text: Steps to configure the domain

blocks.raw: 1. In the Brand organization, navigate to: **Organization Settings > Communication & Gateway > Domains > Configure Domains.**
blocks.text: In the Brand organization, navigate to: Organization Settings > Communication & Gateway > Domains > Configure Domains.

blocks.raw: 2. Select **Config Domain** and enter the details provided by the brand:
blocks.text: Select Config Domain and enter the details provided by the brand:

blocks.raw:
| Field                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| :------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Sender Tag**       | A unique label used to identify the sender profile within the system. It helps you organize and manage different SMS senders.**Note**: Ensure that the sender tag name does not contain any spaces. |
| **Use this for**     | The Purpose for which the domain is configured.  For example- Bulk or transactional.                                                                                                                 |
| **GSM sender ID**    | The alphanumeric sender ID that appears as the “From” name when SMS are delivered over GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) networks.For example - BANKXYZ                                 |
| **GSM Sender Name**  | An alphanumeric name used inside the system to identify the GSM Sender ID. This is not shown to recipients.  For example -  BANKXYZ                                                                  |
| **CDMA Sender ID**   | The sender ID used for CDMA networks, typically a short code or numeric sender. For example: 57575, 56767.                                                                                          |
| **CDMA Sender Name** | A  name used to identify the CDMA Sender ID within the system.                                                                                                                                       |

blocks.raw: ## Configuring SMS priority settings
blocks.text: Configuring SMS priority settings

blocks.raw: When multiple sender IDs are available for a brand, setting a domain priority determines which domain is used to send communications. You can set the priority separately for Bulk SMS and for Transactional (High) SMS.
blocks.text: When multiple sender IDs are available for a brand, setting a domain priority determines which domain is used to send communications. You can set the priority separately for Bulk SMS and for Transactional (High) SMS.

blocks.raw: Steps to configure the domain priority
blocks.text: Steps to configure the domain priority

blocks.raw:
1. In InTouch, select the brand for which you want to set the domain priority. Then navigate to Organization Settings > **Communication & Gateway** > **Domains** > **Domain Gateway Mapping**.
2. On the Mapping page, under Sms Domain - Gateway Mapping:
   1. To set the priority for BulkSMS, select **Update Bulk Priorities**.
   2. To set the priority for Transactional (High) SMS, select **Update High Priorities**.
3. In the priority table, navigate to the domain you want to send messages from.
4. In the **Priority** section, select the + icon for the domain and drag it to the top.
5. Select **Save**.

Then navigate to Organization Settings > Communication & Gateway > Domains > Domain Gateway Mapping.On the Mapping page, under Sms Domain - Gateway Mapping:To set the priority for BulkSMS, select Update Bulk Priorities.To set the priority for Transactional (High) SMS, select Update High Priorities.In the priority table, navigate to the domain you want to send messages from.In the Priority section, select the + icon for the domain and drag it to the top.Select Save.

blocks.raw: The priority is now updated for the selected Sender ID under the selected brand. When you send a communication, it will be sent from the sender ID that is set as the priority, regardless of the other domains listed in the table.
